Same with "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Relic of Legends"}},{"insert":", with our high amount of Legendary creatures we often get 3+ out of this on  later turns.

"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Draw:"},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"				Again, we need a lot of stuff to consistently threaten a win by turn 7, thats why this deck runs a lot draw engines.  All the standard ones in our color identy are included. 
				Stand outs are "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Enduring Innocence"}},{"insert":" and "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Welcoming Vampire"}},{"insert":" (I only run one), because we run over 20 creatures including our commander with power 2 or less. (Could still argue to cut these)
				"},{"insert":{"card-link":"Lórien Revealed"}},{"insert":" is expensive, but when we really need cards we can afford it, because of our ramp and if not its basically a land.

"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Removal:"},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
"},{"insert":"				To make this janky deck run as non-janky and explosive as possible we run alot of draw and ramp and our suite of removal suffers the most from that decision. 
				That's why the removal we do run either: targets permanents in general like "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Stroke of Midnight"}},{"insert":" or has other uses like "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Heliod's Intervention"}},{"insert":", "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Otawara, Soaring City"}},{"insert":" or "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Loran of the Third Path"}},{"insert":" 
				We only run asymmetric board wipes like "},{"insert":{"card-link":"The Battle of Bywater"}},{"insert":" or "},{"insert":{"card-link":"Dusk // Dawn"}},{"insert":" to leave our board untouched. We effecivly only run two creatures effected by these board wipes.

"},{"attributes":{"bold":true},"insert":"Protection"},{"insert":": "},{"attributes":{"list":"bullet"},"insert":"
